newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spot down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spot down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Tuesday with rumours that the central bank would ban state commercial banks from trading on the repo market helping early-maturing contracts to stay at high levels, traders said.
Central bank officials declined to comment.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.00 percent from 14.98 percent on Monday.
Total turnover fell to 7.24 million lots from 11.95 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the market was influenced by rumours the on-going bank meeting in Beijing was discussing a ban on state commercial banks from trading T-bill repurchase papers.
"If the rumours prove to be true, the repo market turnover will drop with supply deceasing," said a trader. " The rates, in particular those for early-maturing contracts, will rise."
Contracts on Shanghai's T-bill spot market ended down due to rumours that the commercial banks would also be banned from trading on the T-bill secondary market, traders said.
The most active three-year bond that matures in 1999 fell to 102.93 yuan from 103.30 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.43 million lots from 2.14 million.
Traders said that if the commercial banks were banned from trading on the T-bill secondary market, liquidity on the market would fall, which encouraged investors to sell today.
But they said coupons of the existing contracts were high due to China's sharply falling inflation and prices were likely to find continued support.
